site.name: Hanagumi Atelier — Kyoto
site.concept: A small Kyoto studio for woodblock-informed graphic design, paper goods, and editorial typography.

card_pattern: Cards are plain kraft-toned panels with a 1px sumi rule along the top edge, generous internal padding (top-heavy), and a single small kamon stamp seated in the lower-right corner at ~24px. Titles set in Shippori Mincho, metadata in small-caps Inter, body in Inter at 1.75 line-height. No drop-shadows, no rounded corners — the corners are square and the negative space inside the card does the work.
design_rules: Asymmetric composition with at least 30% of every screen left deliberately empty. Wagara patterns appear only as low-opacity (8–12%) tiled bands; kamon appear as discrete seals — never repeated, never decorative filler. Typography leans on the thick-thin contrast of Shippori Mincho for titles against quiet, generously-leaded Inter body.

pages.title: Hanagumi Atelier — A Kyoto studio for print, paper, and type
pages.content_brief: Off-center hero with the studio name set in Shippori Mincho, balanced by a small umebachi seal and a wide negative field. Beneath it, a brief statement: 'Founded in Nishijin in 2014 by Mariko Adachi and Sōta Kuwabara, Hanagumi works on book design, paper goods, and identity systems for cultural clients across Kansai.' Three featured projects teased as plain text-cards: a monograph for Raku Museum, stationery for Ippodo Tea, and a wayfinding system for the Kamigamo shrine forest walk.

pages.title: Studio — Hanagumi Atelier
pages.content_brief: Studio history and philosophy. Two narrow columns: the left a short essay on the influence of Hiroshige's Kisokaidō series and the discipline of negative space (ma) on the studio's approach to layout; the right a chronology — 2014 founded above Tomi-no-Kōji street, 2017 first Tokyo Art Book Fair, 2019 Mainichi Design Award (silver, book category), 2022 expansion into a second-floor workroom on Aneyakōji. Closes with a portrait paragraph for each of the four current members.

pages.title: Works — Selected projects 2016–2024
pages.content_brief: A vertical index of selected projects. Each entry is a row: year (right-aligned, small-caps), client, project title in Shippori Mincho, one-line description. Examples: '2024 — Raku Museum — Four Hundred Years of Black Glaze (catalogue, 312pp)', '2023 — Ippodo Tea — Sencha box series (six SKUs, letterpress)', '2022 — Kamigamo Shrine — Forest path wayfinding', '2020 — Heibonsha — Kisokaidō Reread (book design)'. A short paragraph above the index frames the studio's range.

pages.title: Process — How we work
pages.content_brief: Four-step process described in narrow text columns: 'Reading' (research and material study), 'Drafting' (paper dummies, hand-set proofs), 'Refining' (press tests with our regular printers Benrido and Shinanobashi Insatsu), 'Delivery' (production oversight and archival deposit). A pull-quote in display weight: 'A page should feel inhabited before it is read.' — Mariko Adachi, 2021.

pages.title: Journal — Notes from the studio
pages.content_brief: Short-form writing from the studio. Five entries listed reverse-chronologically: 'On the seigaiha grid' (March 2024, on tessellation in book endpapers), 'A week at Awagami' (November 2023, mill visit on Shikoku), 'Type specimens for Mincho-derived Latin' (August 2023), 'Why we still proof on newsprint' (May 2023), 'Hiroshige's snow' (January 2023). Each entry shows a date, title, and three-line excerpt.

pages.title: Contact & Visit — Hanagumi Atelier
pages.content_brief: Address: 二階, 384 Aneyakōji-dōri Tominokōji nishi-iru, Nakagyō-ku, Kyōto 604-8091. Hours: Tuesday–Friday 11:00–18:00, by appointment. Direct line: studio@hanagumi.kyoto. Inquiries for new commissions reviewed quarterly; next intake closes 30 September. Brief travel note: five minutes north of Karasuma-Oike station, exit 2; the entrance is a narrow machiya doorway between a kimono lining shop and a coffee stand — ring the upper bell.
